# Operation Input requirements and read scope

<!-- Generated by reader-references.mjs from spec/operations/input-authority.md; edit the owner, not this view. -->

Start with the [Pack field guide](./pack-fields.md) for task-oriented explanations.

<a id="operation-input-requirements-and-authority" />

## Applicability

This page applies only to the
[operation-scoped Core](./operation-format.md), Revision
`1.0-alpha.2`. Existing Revision `1.0-alpha.1` keeps the global required,
binding visibility and removal rules in Input declarations
and Inputs and Secrets.

### Operation-specific Input admission {#pr-req-0381---operation-specific-input-admission}

Global declarations MUST define identity and protection, not execution
requiredness. Each operation's required list MUST be satisfied in its own
context before Hook launch; optional absence MUST NOT block admission.
An empty required list MUST impose no Input completeness prerequisite.
Absence MUST remain distinct from a bound zero-length payload.

| Operation | Requirement and read context |
| --- | --- |
| Action | Pinned current active bindings |
| Capture | Pinned current active bindings |
| Restore | Validated staged active Snapshot bindings |
| Migration source | Pinned source bindings with explicit active/retained roles |
| Migration target | Staged active target bindings before the Hook |
| Cleanup | Current active/retained bindings with explicit roles |

The Compiler MUST identify missing required references and validate resolvable
roles before side effects. Admission MUST revalidate the exact Revision,
declarations, binding observations, protection and operation requirements in
the serialized admission boundary and pin the accepted context. Optional
presence/absence changes MUST follow plan invalidation rules, not silently
change the context after compilation. Once admitted, later allowed mutations
MUST NOT substitute another payload into the pinned Hook view.

Requirements MUST NOT be replaced by the union of all operations' required
Inputs. There is no Instance-wide readiness predicate for this Core. Inspection
MUST report a selected operation's requirements and missing references; an
unevaluated Snapshot or Migration context MUST be reported as not evaluated,
not satisfied or missing. Trust, launcher availability, recovery guards,
resources, exclusivity and all other admission conditions remain independent.
Input satisfaction MUST NOT be presented as overall execution permission.

Restore MUST evaluate staged state, not target pre-Restore completeness.
Migration whole-chain preflight, target writer uniqueness, mandatory outputs
and explicit declassification remain in force. Hook-free Migration edges
still evaluate their declared requirements. Missing source semantics MUST NOT
be hidden by an empty required list.

### Operation requiredness and binding removal {#pr-req-0382---operation-requiredness-and-binding-removal}

For an Instance whose active Revision selects the new Core, operator removal
of an active binding MUST NOT be refused merely because an operation requires
it. Removal makes those operation requirements unsatisfied. Other mutation,
locking, ownership and authorization checks remain in force. Retained bindings
remain inspectable/exportable/removable and not directly settable by operators.

Sticky Secret protection and explicit declassification rules remain in force.
An allowed deletion ends that binding's continuity without secure-erasure
claims. Requiredness MUST NOT silently become a new protection or retention
policy. An old-format active Revision retains its bound-required removal rule.

New-format Restore MUST NOT impose the old bound-required-to-absent prohibition.
It MUST instead validate the staged state's own Restore requirements and all
independent protection/replacement invariants. A failed Restore MUST NOT remove
bindings or publish a partial replacement.

### Explicit Input read authority {#pr-req-0383---explicit-input-read-authority}

The union of an operation's required and optional references MUST be its maximum
Pactrun-provided Input read authority. Undeclared references MUST NOT be exposed
through Session descriptors, enumeration, lookup, payload streaming or authority
resolution. An empty declaration MUST grant no Input read authority. Guessing
an identity, handle or locator MUST NOT bypass the grant or disclose whether
an undeclared binding exists. This does not hide public global declarations
inside the installed Revision from a trusted native process.

Only present, authorized bindings MUST receive read-only paths and handles.
An authorized absent optional Input has no payload authority; it MUST NOT be
materialized as an empty file. No undeclared payload may be materialized in
Hook-facing staging merely because Pactrun pinned it internally. Other output
and service authorities remain governed by their own contracts.

Migration transitions may require Pactrun to read an unexposed source internally;
this MUST NOT confer Hook read authority. `produces_target` authorizes declared
output submission and requires successful production, not reading preexisting
target data. Requirement and grant checks MUST use the source/target context,
not an unqualified string-key lookup across both.

Capture MUST still pin and record the complete active and retained managed
binding state, including absence and protection, even when its Hook has no
Input grants. Restore MUST still publish the complete validated replacement.
Neither lifecycle may use the filtered Session view as its authoritative
Snapshot or publication state.

These are Pactrun disclosure boundaries, not native-process sandbox guarantees.
Hook process trust, OS filesystem access, and unrelated ServiceStorage authority
are not restricted by an Input declaration alone.
